text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY TIMES
- Reopening of Mobil's Oso condensate field rescheduled for late this week. Nigeria may lose over $20 million in revenue as result of closure.
- Three people were killed, over 60 hurt in fighting between two southwest Nigerian communities over relocation of local government headquarters at weekend.
- Closure of northern Kaduna oil refinery has pushed up price of kerosene in region to 70 naira from 30 naira per litre (0.22 gallon).
BUSINESS TIMES
- Crude oil allocation for Nigeria's refineries has risen to over 211,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 150,000 bpd.
- Meteorologists say harvests of food crops likely to be below average in Nigeria this year because of unusual weather patterns.
- Strong indications that amount of money being lost to fraud by banks is increasing.
THE GUARDIAN
- Youths in Niger Delta have launched new protest against oil companies working in area, most prominent of which is Royal Dutch/Shell .
- Crude oil allocations to refineries may have been deregulated, with each receiving what it needs according to its actual processing capacity.
- Task force begins arrest of illegal operators of Very Small Aperture Terminal Satellite (V.SAT) services.
- Deputy central bank governor calls for independence for bank to allow it to do job efficiently.
THISDAY

- France's Total has been contracted to run 110,000 bpd Kaduna oil refinery in northern Nigeria for next three years as well as completing turnaround maintenance in contract worth between $160 million and $200 million.
VANGUARD
- Turnaround maintenance of oil refineries may have to wait until next year because government will not release funds until teams of inspectors have completed work, not due to end until October 31.
- Banks move activity to foreign exchange market, shunning treasury bills and money market.
